research.scope: Read-only upstream code/metadata/license inspection; source retained only under /tmp for research. No repo implementation/assets copied or imported; no new dependencies installed; external CPU latency/RAM/accuracy unmeasured.

projects.approach: spaCy PhraseMatcher passes for exact phrases, abbreviations, unigrams, lower-surface forms and partial token matches; Porter stemming/lemmatization, heuristic token-overlap weighting and spaCy word-vector/Jaro similarity resolve partial candidates. EMSI-derived skill IDs provide dictionary linking. Not a trained skill-specific NER model.
projects.requirement_classification: No explicit required/optional/negated/alternative classification in annotate output. Returned text is normalized/transformed; doc_node_id identifies transformed tokens rather than original source character spans.
projects.dictionary_terms: README identifies EMSI database. Root source MIT exists, but no separate source-database license/attribution/version is supplied in inspected repository files. The processing script uses EMSI skills API; source asset permissions/attributions are not proved by code MIT. Official current EMSI/Lightcast endpoints were inaccessible (proxy HTTP403), so no current provider-license claim is made.
projects.remote_behavior: Importing general_params reads CWD skill_db_relax_20.json/token_dist.json or downloads from mutable AnasAito/SkillNER first_release branch and writes CWD. No content-hash/revision pin in default path.

languages.English: Default en_core_web_lg pipeline, English EMSI-derived dictionary and English Porter stemmer
languages.Russian: No Russian skill benchmark or model. Optional user-supplied translator callback translates to English; not native RU support and cannot preserve original offsets automatically.

dependencies.torch: No mandatory PyTorch dependency; spaCy/Thinc CPU approach
dependencies.python: Only generic Python3 classifier; historical dev environment pins Python3.8; Python3.11/3.12 compatibility not executed
dependencies.package: skillNer==1.0.3, latest PyPI release observed 2021-11-07; unbounded runtime dependencies and no requires_python metadata
dependencies.compatibility_risk: Current dependency compatibility not established. Upstream fallback uses jellyfish.jaro_distance; fork changes this to jaro_similarity and modifies scoring. Do not treat fork and upstream as independent algorithms or equal runtime behavior.

projects.benchmark_evidence: Inspected README/source provides examples/demos, not a reproducible SkillSpan precision/recall/F1 or independent Russian evaluation. No external extractor was installed or run in ResumeAnalysis.
projects.resource_notes: No mandatory CUDA. README claims en_core_web_lg download about800MB, an upstream historical statement, not RAM or an observed measurement. Separate pinned spaCy model metadata records actual artifact size below. Python object/dictionary and spaCy vector runtime RAM are unmeasured.
projects.recommendation: Reference-only. No third-party implementation/dictionary/weight copied or imported. Independently authored context-aware rules retain exact source spans and requirement semantics without implicit downloads or heavy dependencies; optional NER needs separate reviewed local assets.

research.scope: Read-only upstream source/metadata research. No third-party implementation, NER weights or new datasets copied into the repository; no dependencies installed; no CPU latency/RAM measured for external projects.

projects.approach: BIO sequence labeling for SKILL and KNOWLEDGE; BERT, SpanBERT and job-domain-adapted JobBERT/JobSpanBERT; separate or multitask models. MaChAmp training scripts/configs, not a maintained lightweight extractor package.
projects.dataset_terms: Repository releases code/data and contains MIT LICENSE; README releases two of three de-identified subsets and requests the SkillSpan paper citation. No separate data license file. Rights in original job advertisements still need review before redistribution.
projects.weight_terms: HF JobBERT skill/knowledge repositories inspected separately; no license declaration or LICENSE file there. The source-repository MIT should not silently be asserted as an asset-specific model grant.

languages.English: Dataset and models explicitly English job-posting task
languages.Russian: No Russian validation or support claim in examined material

projects.compatibility: README retains historical Python 3.6/PyTorch 1.7.0 instructions, notes migration to new MaChAmp (without AllenNLP) in February 2024. Actual modern Python 3.11/3.12 compatibility of upstream experiment runner not tested. Exported BERT token classifier uses standard Transformers BertForTokenClassification (config says 4.26.1).
projects.benchmark_evidence: Paper/README reports domain-adapted models outperform non-adapted and single-task outperforms multitask; no checkpoint-level exact figures verified from paper in this environment. ACL PDF fetch blocked by host allowlist. These are published task claims, not new ResumeAnalysis results.
projects.recommendation: Keep existing pinned SkillSpan benchmark and retained MIT/citation. Do not copy training stack just for CPU extraction; do not infer model asset terms.

projects.approach: Academic Colab notebooks: spaCy LOWER PhraseMatcher dictionary baseline, fine-tuned distilbert-base-uncased token classifier; normalization uses BM25 + semantic matching. README calls cross-encoder reranking, but examined normalization notebook imports SentenceTransformer(all-MiniLM-L6-v2), so README and actual notebook deserve separate validation.

source_license.finding: No LICENSE/NOTICE in complete repository tree. README License section says academic purposes as part of CS685 at UMass Amherst; this is not an open-source redistribution grant.

research.decision: Prefer an independently authored lightweight rules/phrase recognizer + context/requirements layer with preserved baseline. Optional NER should be gated behind an explicit asset license/provenance manifest. None of the inspected small JobBERT assets has a verified asset license; the one explicitly licensed multilingual model is large and unsuitable as an unmeasured default.
